Where it began

MS Dhoni was born in Ranchi on 7 July 1981, the youngest of three in his family. At DAV Jawahar Vidya Mandir he started out as a football goalkeeper, until his coach, Keshav Banerjee, steered him towards cricket. He swapped one pair of gloves for another and never looked back.

His family actually spell the name Dhauni. A slip on his school certificates turned it into Dhoni, and the family never managed to get it put right. Cricket has spelled it that way ever since.

The player

He kept wicket for the Commando club in his teens and was in the Bihar side at eighteen. For a couple of years he combined cricket with a job as a travelling ticket examiner on the railways at Kharagpur.

His Test debut came against Sri Lanka in Chennai in December 2005, and his first Test hundred at Faisalabad in 2006. In 90 Tests he made 4,876 runs at 38.09, with six hundreds, 33 fifties and a best of 224, the most Test runs by any Indian wicketkeeper. Behind the stumps he held 256 catches and made 38 stumpings. He captained India in 60 Tests, winning 27, and in 2009 his side reached the top of the ICC Test rankings for the first time. In his last Test, at Melbourne in December 2014, he made nine dismissals.

What made him special

Nothing about him came from the coaching manual. He held the bat low on the handle and drove full balls hard towards long-on and long-off, and he ran between the wickets as fast as anyone. Above all he stayed calm, which earned him the name Captain Cool, and in Chennai the fans simply call him Thala, the leader.

Purists were never sure about his wicketkeeping technique. His hands were so fast, though, that it rarely seemed to matter. In a one-day match against the West Indies he completed a stumping in 0.08 seconds, the fastest ever recorded.

Away from the middle

He led India to the T20 World Cup in 2007, the World Cup in 2011 and the Champions Trophy in 2013. He has the Khel Ratna, the Padma Shri and the Padma Bhushan, and entered the ICC Hall of Fame in 2025. The Indian Army made him an honorary Lieutenant Colonel in the Parachute Regiment in 2011, and in 2015 he qualified as a paratrooper. In 2023 India retired the No.7 shirt in his honour.

He went on playing for Chennai Super Kings in the IPL and led them again in 2025. A film of his life, M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story, came out in 2016. He lives on his farm in Ranchi and loves his motoring, with a collection of bikes and cars to prove it.

And finally

He bowled in Tests without taking a wicket, which suggests he was right to keep the gloves on. His famous helicopter shot was not his own invention, either. He learned it from Santosh Lal, a friend from his childhood.
